title: Regression Algorithms
description: Model continuous and discrete targets with different regression types.
content:
**Linear regression** is a method used to model the relationships between one or more independent variables and a continuous dependent variable - for example, predicting the price of an apartment from its size and location.

The most common approach for estimating parameters in linear regression is **least squares estimation**, which aims at searching the parameter values that minimize the residual sum of squares.

**Logistic regression** estimates the probability of a binary outcome based on one or more independent variables. It uses the sigmoid function to constrain the output to the range from 0 to 1. Despite its name, it is typically used for classification: the predicted probability is compared against a threshold to assign one of the two classes.

The most common approach for estimating parameters in logistic regression is the **method of maximum likelihood**, which aims at maximizing the log-likelihood function.

> Key differences between the two methods:
> • Target - linear regression predicts a continuous dependent variable, while logistic regression estimates the probability of a binary outcome.
> • Output range - linear regression can output any real value, while logistic regression constrains its output from 0 to 1 via the sigmoid function.
> • Parameter estimation - linear regression commonly uses least squares (minimizing the residual sum of squares), while logistic regression commonly uses maximum likelihood (maximizing the log-likelihood function).
